The authors performed the derivation, computation, and experimental design in a 2D geometry where all physical quantities are invariant along the third dimension.
The carpet cloak is equivalent to a bent electromagnetic space that is transformed from the original flat electromagnetic space via a specific coordinate transformation.
The relative permittivity and permeability of the carpet cloak can be obtained from the coordinate transformation.
In the virtual space, the trajectory of the charged particle is bent while the time remains the same as in the physical space, resulting in an increased speed by a factor of 1 + (τ/κ)^2.
For a charged particle velocity of 0.81c in the physical space, only transition radiation is observed as the particle enters, crosses, and exits the cloak.
For a charged particle velocity of 0.98c in the physical space, both transition radiation and Cherenkov radiation are observed inside the cloak.

The authors designed a layered metamaterial structure composed of air and Zn-Ni-Fe composite in a Teflon background to realize the required anisotropic permittivity and permeability of the carpet cloak.
The designed carpet cloak had constitutive parameters of μu = 1.32 + 0.02i, εv = 3.49 + 0.05i, and μz = 1.26 + 0.0006i.
The authors simulated the scattering field excited by a 1 GHz current passing through the designed carpet cloak and showed good agreement with the ideal case.
The authors proposed to use a microwave experiment with an antenna array to simulate the radiation from a charged particle and verify their findings.
The asymmetric Cherenkov radiation pattern observed inside the carpet cloak is a result of the anisotropic permittivity and permeability of the cloak.
The asymmetry between photons and charged particles in transformation optics reveals a fundamental limitation of this approach in cloaking charged particle dynamics.

The authors used a 2D line charged particle to model the current density, as the 2D geometry allows the radiation to be in the transverse magnetic (TM) field, which is compatible with the carpet cloak design.
The authors discretized the current segments in the virtual space into finite dipole arrays to facilitate the analysis of the radiation patterns.
Reflection of the fields at the ground plane was taken into account by using equivalent image sources.
